capability.description: Provide the bounded crawl execution engine behind Time to Crawl's CrawlerEnginePort without building a generic crawler from scratch.
constraints: Preserve TTC policy and scheduler authority outside the engine.
Support HTTP crawling and a bounded browser/dynamic path through adapters.
Keep live engine selection blocked until the isolation and matched bakeoff gates are satisfied.
non_goals: Build a custom crawler, queue, or browser pool when a mature engine can be adapted.

searches.query: Pukujan repositories containing an existing reusable crawler engine or crawler runtime

receipts.note: Owner repository inventory was searched for an existing internal crawler engine before considering bespoke implementation.

searches.rationale: No separate internal crawler engine was identified that could replace the external-engine bakeoff.

searches.query: maintained Python crawler framework HTTP Playwright request queue scheduler robots retries

receipts.note: Concrete Crawlee for Python candidate used by Time to Crawl issue #8 and candidate engine pins.
Concrete mature Scrapy baseline used by Time to Crawl issue #8 and candidate engine pins.

tradeoffs.fitness: Strong fit for the required HTTP plus Playwright composition path, with queues, retries, routing, storage abstractions, and browser support.
tradeoffs.maintenance: Maintained external framework and the leading candidate recorded by the adopter.
tradeoffs.license: Must remain part of the dependency and SBOM review before activation.
tradeoffs.security: The engine cannot own TTC policy or serve as an SSRF boundary; all egress remains mediated outside the adapter.
tradeoffs.extensibility: Fits behind CrawlerEnginePort without making framework internals authoritative.
tradeoffs.integration_cost: Requires a real adapter plus isolation/security conformance work before live activation.
tradeoffs.performance: Must be compared on matched fixtures and bounded real canaries rather than assumed from feature breadth.
material_reasons: It plausibly covers the required engine capability without a custom crawler.
Selection still depends on objective bakeoff evidence and the isolation gate.

tradeoffs.fitness: Production-mature crawler baseline with scheduler/downloader middleware, pipelines, duplicate filtering, pause/resume, and throttling.
tradeoffs.maintenance: Mature maintained external project and the adopter's reference baseline.
tradeoffs.license: Must remain part of the dependency and SBOM review before activation.
tradeoffs.security: As with Crawlee, framework filtering cannot replace TTC's external authorization and isolation boundary.
tradeoffs.extensibility: Can be adapted behind CrawlerEnginePort while preserving TTC-owned policy and provenance semantics.
tradeoffs.integration_cost: Requires matched adapter implementation and browser-path integration analysis.
tradeoffs.performance: Must be compared against Crawlee on the same correctness, recovery, security, observability, and resource cases.
material_reasons: It is a credible mature alternative rather than a category label.
It provides an objective fallback/baseline for the engine decision.

probes.rationale: The adopter has a fake-engine bakeoff harness, but the real Crawlee adapter and live bakeoff remain blocked until Time to Crawl issue #4 isolation passes; issue #8 intentionally keeps engine selection open.
The matched real Scrapy bakeoff is intentionally deferred behind the same isolation gate; selecting an engine from prose or the fake harness would violate the adopter's own acceptance rule.

decision.rationale: Reuse is mandatory and two concrete mature engines are identified, but the adopter correctly keeps the final choice open until the matched live bakeoff can run. Building a generic crawler is not authorized.
residual_uncertainty: Which engine better satisfies TTC's isolation, recovery, browser, provenance, and resource constraints under matched tests.
reconsideration_triggers: Time to Crawl issue #4 isolation becomes green and the real Crawlee-vs-Scrapy bakeoff can run.
Both mature candidates fail a concrete required CrawlerEnginePort capability under matched evidence.
